sources.semantic_operation_reviewed: FTS5 build enablement, grammar, Unicode61, external-content lifecycle, ranking, excerpts, integrity, rebuild, tokenizer API
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 amalgamation support starts at 3.9.0; build enablement is conditional. External content queries a same-database object and requires application synchronization. Default Unicode61 uses Unicode 6.1 L*/N*/Co categories and remove_diacritics=1; option 2 fixes a legacy multi-diacritic case. Category prose alone does not capture the combining-diacritic implementation exception (E15/E19). Contentless-delete starts in 3.43.0, supports DELETE/INSERT OR REPLACE and all-column UPDATE, and excludes the special delete command. External-content REPLACE uses ABORT. Rank=1 enables external-content integrity comparison; discrepancies produce SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB. Rebuild is unavailable for contentless tables. BM25 returns a real score with smaller being better. Snippet bound is tokens, 1–64, not the final custom 160-scalar limit. FTS secure-delete defaults to 0; enabling it affects format compatibility with pre-3.42.0 readers.
sources.applicability: Governs the preferred released-component proposal and old-plan corrections; does not establish any deployed binary or schema.

sources.semantic_operation_reviewed: Same-database write atomicity and BEGIN IMMEDIATE fence
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: One simultaneous write transaction, multiple readers. BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write transaction immediately or returns SQLITE_BUSY; existing read transactions see a historical snapshot. Commit may be busy and may require retry; errors can roll back a statement or whole transaction.
sources.applicability: Supports trigger/outbox transactions and cutover inference; not a cross-store atomicity guarantee.

material_findings.title: The final blanket combining-mark separator claim is false for the proposed Unicode61 configuration

final_locators.detail: Default category policy treats combining marks outside those token categories as separators
R3 is claimed resolved at proposal level

authored_source_locators.detail: reviser_direct_rechecks V02 repeats the separator claim
V02 governing condition repeats the claim

material_findings.finding: Unicode61 has an in-token diacritic exception beyond the L*/N*/Co category test. Recognized combining modifiers such as U+0301 continue the token, and remove_diacritics=2 removes the mark instead of ending the token. The final states the opposite as its tokenization policy.
material_findings.counterexample: ca + U+0301 + fe becomes the single FTS token cafe, not ca and fe. A reviewer-only in-memory SQLite 3.46.1 check independently observed that token and cafe-query match. Tantivy SimpleTokenizer splits non-alphanumeric combining marks before folding, so this is a meaningful comparator distinction.
material_findings.materiality: Accents and token/phrase boundaries are explicit S1 obligations. A wrong declared boundary changes expected lexical matches and prospective oracle outcomes; general caution about canonical equivalence does not qualify this positive blanket statement.
material_findings.lineage: Introduced in the reviser explanation and V02 while addressing a legitimate R3 incompleteness. The predecessor uncertainty about analyzer parity remains supported.
material_findings.scope_limit: The evidence proves the bounded recognized-diacritic exception in released SQLite 3.43.0 source and a local 3.46.1 corroborating witness. It does not establish universal normalization or a deployed application configuration.

material_findings.classification: material incomplete / unsupported consequential completeness rule
material_findings.title: The Tantivy completeness rule does not bind its watermark to the loaded reader/searcher snapshot

final_locators.detail: Commit publication is used as the reader-visibility boundary
Candidate commit, durable watermark and active marker
Compare applied-through watermark with latest source sequence before calling results complete

material_findings.finding: Tantivy 0.26.2 commits publish index state, but IndexReader lends the last loaded Searcher. Its default reload is asynchronous and Manual needs an explicit reload. The final defines writer-applied and source sequences, without defining reader reload/acquisition or proving that the searcher used for a query has loaded that committed sequence.
material_findings.counterexample: An existing reader/searcher is at sequence 10. The outbox worker indexes a new matching note, commits sequence 11 and records applied-through=11; SQLite latest sequence is 11. Before the default delayed reload occurs, the final watermark equality succeeds while the searcher still uses sequence 10 and omits the note. Under Manual or a retained old Searcher, this can persist. Fetching current source text cannot discover a missing candidate.
material_findings.materiality: The original plan expressly prohibits presenting partial results as complete and requires update/recovery/rebuild behavior. This is a published-versus-loaded operation condition within the required alternative, not an invented deployment requirement or a demand for a running application.
material_findings.lineage: The publication-only boundary is inherited from discovery/draft/source records; the critic did not identify it. Final R1 fixes the source-write/cutover race, but its additional completeness rule leaves this separate reader condition unresolved.
material_findings.scope_limit: This is a source-backed architectural counterexample; no Tantivy dependency was built or run. The write fence and per-generation retention are otherwise sound proposal-level corrections.

material_findings.classification: material incomplete / inapplicable proposed API operation
material_findings.title: Accepted one-term quoted input is routed to a PhraseQuery constructor that requires multiple terms

final_locators.detail: Any balanced nonempty quoted segment is accepted subject to bounds
Quoted segment becomes a phrase
Build a zero-slop Tantivy PhraseQuery from its analyzed terms

material_findings.finding: The bounded language permits a one-token quoted phrase such as "café". The specified Tantivy operation constructs a PhraseQuery for quoted spans, but 0.26.2 PhraseQuery::new and new_with_offset_and_slop require strictly more than one term and assert otherwise. The final supplies no singleton disposition or lowering.
material_findings.counterexample: "café" is balanced, nonempty and below both limits. The proposed analyzer emits cafe, one term. The prescribed PhraseQuery construction hits the documented/asserted arity restriction.
material_findings.materiality: Quoted input and malformed-query behavior are explicit S1 and exact-plan obligations. The plan presents a backend mapping for accepted input that is not applicable to an ordinary valid case. This is not merely a request for more implementation code.
material_findings.lineage: The generic typed-phrase proposal is inherited; the reviser made the mapping explicit while claiming R3 resolved. Its V05 source locator includes the constructor region but omits the arity condition in the recorded summary.
material_findings.scope_limit: No crash in a nonexistent application is asserted; the source proves the proposed operation is incomplete for this accepted domain.
